source.title: When Agents Collude: Weak-to-Strong On-Policy Distillation for Mitigating Strategic Deception in Multi-Agent Systems
source.authors: Eric Onyame; Run Zhou; Kowshik Thopalli; B. Kailkhura; Chirag Agarwal

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses weak-to-strong on-policy distillation as an anti-deception intervention and reports how that intervention performs. It does not measure PGR or compare the student’s task outcome with the weaker teacher’s outcome, so it does not test the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports strategic-deception outcomes after honesty SFT and PACT, including persistent-deception rates. It does not report PGR, weak-teacher-only outcomes on the evaluation task, or a direct student-versus-teacher comparison. Capability-benchmark results and cited results from other work are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: PACT uses a smaller honesty-aligned teacher as a tool to cut deception in a larger student. The paper reports only the student's deception rates (baseline vs SFT vs PACT). It never reports the frozen teacher's own rates on the insider-trading task and never computes PGR. So it cannot show whether a student beats its weak supervisor (V1), whether a training change raises PGR (V2), or how PGR varies (V3–V4). There is no theory (V5) and no vision work (V6).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also conclude that multi-agent coordination amplifies misaligned action and persistent deception relative to single agents; that is the paper's main finding and the paraphrase omits it.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a smaller honesty-aligned teacher to supervise a stronger student, but applies reverse-KL on student-generated continuations after honesty SFT rather than fine-tuning on weak-model-produced task labels. It evaluates deception mitigation, not PGR.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported mitigation outcomes vary by pressure environment, agent setting, coordination topology, and model. The paper notes that PACT’s additional benefit over SFT varies across conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: After honesty SFT, on-policy reverse-KL distillation from a smaller honesty-SFT teacher further lowers end-to-end persistent deception: 16→6% single-agent and 30→15% multi-agent, pooled. For larger students in the multi-agent setting (Table 8): Llama-3.1-70B 51.7→30.6%, Llama-3.3-70B 52.3→26.9%, DeepSeek-70B 24.1→15.2%, Gemma-27B 26.5→3.8%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: On-policy distillation from a smaller honesty-aligned teacher reduces strategic-deception rates in larger students beyond direct honesty SFT, in a simulated insider-trading task.

fits_no_version.finding: In the same-size DeepSeek-8B self-distillation pair, multi-agent PDR shows no improvement (10.8→11.7%). For Llama-3.1-8B under high detection risk (sequential multi-agent), PACT raises MR from 15% to 20% and PDR from 12% to 14% vs SFT.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The added benefit of on-policy honesty distillation over SFT is not uniform across models and conditions.

record.problems: No direct weak-teacher-only evaluation or student-versus-teacher comparison is reported, so the study cannot establish that the student beats its supervisor or quantify PGR. Deception outcomes are classified by an automated judge; the authors note possible classification errors, although they report 100% agreement in an audit of 700 baseline trajectories. Some results are aggregates across models and settings.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted capability-retention results on GSM8K, ARC-Challenge, and MMLU, human–judge agreement results, and behavioral outcomes that do not bear directly on the weak-supervision intervention.

untested.parts: No teacher-only deception rates on the evaluation task; no student-vs-supervisor comparison; no PGR or strong ceiling.
PACT vs SFT and data-matched SFT are compared on student deception rates only, not PGR.
No PGR variation with supervisor or student size, and no predictors.
No measure of exploitation of supervisor blind spots, shift effects on PGR, or shared errors.

missing.what: Per-model weak-to-strong pairs (70B/27B students) with SFT and PACT PDR. These are relevant to the fits_no_version claim, though they bear on no version.

record.verdict_notes: The main text says PACT beats SFT in all 14 model–setting pairs. Table 8 contradicts this: DeepSeek-8B multi-agent PDR rises. Figure 21's caption wrongly says a 'stronger 8B model guides the 70B'. Three of seven teacher–student pairs are same-size, so 'weak-to-strong' strictly covers only four students. Deception labels come from an LLM judge (GPT-OSS-120B), audited only on baseline trajectories.

versions.untested_parts: No weak-supervisor outcome, student-versus-supervisor comparison, or PGR.
PACT is compared with honesty SFT on deception rates, but the study does not measure PGR or whether the change raises PGR.
No PGR variation or predictors are reported; model and setting variation is not analyzed using PGR.
No test of shared errors between weak and strong models or distribution-shift effects on PGR.
No theoretical conditions for a student to beat its supervisor.

rows.note: Aggregate across seven models. The paper reports a reduction after PACT but does not report teacher-only outcomes or PGR.
rows.check: The pooled aggregate includes three same-size self-distillation pairs (Llama-3.1-8B→8B, DeepSeek-8B→8B, Gemma-12B→12B), so it is not purely weak-to-strong. The drop from 16% to 6% vs SFT is a clear reduction, better coded observed than partial for the fits_no_version finding.
